description: The valid-option transfer taken at the SECOND slot of the option table, stated in full: a re-entry carrying CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1, an AID of DFHENTER and OPTIONI '2 ' - a digit in byte 1, a space in byte 2 - which is the UNPADDED form of an option and therefore the form that exercises every step of the normalisation at app/cbl/COADM01C.cbl:117-125. Line 87's IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is false, so the ELSE at 91 runs: RECEIVE-MENU-SCREEN at 92, then the ordered three-way EVALUATE EIBAID at 93-103, whose FIRST arm is DFHENTER, whose second is DFHPF3 and whose WHEN OTHER is last, so PROCESS-ENTER-KEY is what runs - the arm case01's prose assigns to this case. The first two arms compare distinct bytes, so which of them runs is decided by the byte itself; what the source order guarantees is that the WHEN OTHER at 99-102 can never pre-empt either of them (gate G30). The five normalisation steps with every intermediate value: (1) the descending scan at 117-121 tests before it varies, so from WS-IDX 2 it finds byte 2 blank and 2 not equal to 1 and continues, then at 1 finds byte 1 is '2' and stops with WS-IDX = 1; (2) line 122 sends OPTIONI(1:WS-IDX) - one character here, because WS-IDX resolved to 1 - into WS-OPTION-X, declared PIC X(02) JUST RIGHT at line 45, so the character lands at the RIGHTMOST position and the field is space-filled on the LEFT, giving ' 2' and never '2 '; (3) line 123's INSPECT REPLACING ALL ' ' BY '0' turns that into '02'; (4) line 124 moves it into WS-OPTION PIC 9(02), which is 2; (5) line 125 echoes WS-OPTION into OPTIONO as '02'. A left-justifying receiver would instead produce '20', which is past the count and would be rejected, so the direction of the fill is the entire difference between a transfer and an error message. The map already agrees with the receiver - app/bms/COADM01.bms:145-149 declares OPTION with ATTRB=(FSET,IC,NORM,NUM,UNPROT) and JUSTIFY=(RIGHT,ZERO), so the terminal itself would right-justify and zero-fill - which makes the program's own normalisation belt and braces rather than the only line of defence; it is reproduced because the program performs it, not because it is needed. The pre-padded shape, whose scan stops at byte 2 without ever decrementing, is delivered by case06 and case18, both of which send '05' and are rejected for exceeding the count, and case03 and case07 deliver this same unpadded shape at subscript 1; case08 delivers '1 ' through an option table whose entry is DUMMY-prefixed and so takes the fall-through this case must not take. The guard at 127-129 is evaluated in source order and every term is false: WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC is false, WS-OPTION > CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT is false because app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy:20 declares that count 4 and this is 2, and WS-OPTION = ZEROS is false - so no message is composed, SEND-MENU-SCREEN is not performed from 133, and WS-ERR-FLG stays 'N'. Line 137's IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON therefore holds, and line 138 reference-modifies the first five characters of CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION). THAT SUBSCRIPT IS WHAT THIS CASE EXISTS TO PIN. Subscript 2 addresses the second OCCURS entry, which app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy:29-32 declares as option number 2, 'User Add (Security)                ' and 'COUSR01C'; in Java that entry sits at position 1, one less than the subscript. Both directions of an off-by-one land on a real entry at this element, which is what makes it worth pinning: reading the table at position 2 returns 'COUSR02C' and at position 0 returns 'COUSR00C', so a shift transfers to a program that genuinely exists instead of running off the table and announcing itself (gate G33). At subscript 1, which case03 and case07 pin, an over-correction runs off the front and throws, so the two elements catch different mistakes and neither alone is sufficient; an accessor that returned the first entry whatever the subscript satisfies case07 and fails this case. The first five characters are 'COUSR' and are not 'DUMMY', so the transfer arm runs. Lines 139-141 make EXACTLY THREE mutations to the communication area, in source order: CDEMO-FROM-TRANID becomes 'CA00', CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM becomes 'COADM01C', and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT becomes zero, so COUSR01C sees ENTER and paints rather than validating. Every other one of the sixteen fields is echoed byte for byte, which is the assertion of statelessness (gate G37): COADM01C reads no other context field and writes no other, and the state travels in the payload rather than in a session. The XCTL at 142-145 DOES specify COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), so the whole 160-byte area of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy is handed to COUSR01C - unlike the sign-on transfer at 165-167, which names only a program and passes no communication area at all; the two are not interchangeable and case10 pins the other one. The target reaches the client as a response field instead of a control transfer, which is what XCTL becomes in a stateless translation (gate G40). An XCTL never returns, and that is what the rest of this expectation is about. Lines 147-154 sit after the inner END-IF on line 146, so they are TEXTUALLY reachable and are kept out only by the transfer never coming back: a translation that returned from the transfer arm and fell through would blank WS-MESSAGE at 147, move DFHGREEN over the map's COLOR=RED at 148, compose the two-operand STRING at 149-153 into the message and send it at 154, attaching that composed text to a SUCCESSFUL transfer - which COADM01C never emits. That is the single most likely defect on this path, so its absence is asserted positively rather than merely left unstated: the one expected message is the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE of line 38 still holding the spaces line 79 put in it, and the text composed at 149-153 is quoted NOWHERE in this file - deliberately, so that a search for that text across the fixture tree finds case08, the case that does emit it, and not this one. Neither is anything repainted. SEND-MENU-SCREEN is not performed, so its POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at 174 paints no title, transaction, program, date or time, its BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS at 175 composes none of the twelve option lines, and the empty send list is a positive assertion of exactly that; the EXEC CICS RETURN at 107-110 is not reached either, which is why the termination is XCTL and not RETURN_TRANSID. With no send there is no ScreenSend to carry an attribute or a reset signal, so no attribute is declared and none may be: the error-message colour stays the COLOR=RED that app/bms/COADM01.bms:154-157 declares and common.BmsAttributes reproduces as DFHRED, the DFHGREEN of line 148 is the only attribute byte the program ever writes and it belongs to the path this case does not take, and the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COADM1AO at line 89 that a reset signal would report is inside the ENTER branch alone, which case02 pins. The normalised OPTIONO of '02' is likewise asserted at the unit rather than here, because a transfer sends no map for it to travel on. nextMapset and nextMap are deliberately NOT declared: neither XCTL names a map - line 143 names only the option's program name and line 166 only CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM - and which screen COUSR01C paints is COUSR01C's decision, made after this program has ended, so naming the screen being left would be the one answer that is certainly wrong. The map and mapset this run did touch are COADM1A of COADM01, at the RECEIVE on 191-197, and they are recorded here in prose rather than as an expectation for that reason. Also declared, and unread by the program, are OPTN005I through OPTN012I: BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS composes only lines 1 to 4 because the count is 4, and the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COADM1AO that would reset the map is at line 89 inside the ENTER branch ONLY and does not run on a re-entry, so those eight lines are delivered as the spaces their INITIAL=' ' leaves them holding. They are stated explicitly so that the no-reset state is well defined rather than accidental, and as spaces rather than low values precisely because low values are the marker of the reset that did not happen. Only OPTIONI is read. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the timestamp COADM01C's own version footer at line 267 carries, so the instant is anchored in the source rather than chosen; all twenty cases in this directory pin that same instant and name US-ASCII explicitly rather than leaving a code page to a platform default. This path paints no header, so the instant changes nothing it asserts; it is declared all the same so that one clock governs the whole directory. Every expected value above is STATICALLY DERIVED - arrived at by structured reading of the COBOL paragraph that produces it and cross-checked against the 160-byte layout of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, the option table of app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy, the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY and the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COADM01.bms - and NONE of it was captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy program, which is empirically impossible here: no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from the repository. ParityCase's own class documentation is the authoritative statement of that provenance, and the substitution of provenance - and of provenance alone, since the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand - is escalated for explicit confirmation rather than silently absorbed (risk R-A).
